# A DELIBERATE CONFLICT, LEFT IN — AND CORRECTED SINCE #3.
#
# #3 reported this as doc-vs-code: "DESIGN.md promises a 30-day grid, the shipped
# route takes a caller-supplied window". Checked line by line, that is WRONG in
# the direction that made it sound better. The route is
# `int historyDays = 30` (HabitRoutes.cs:68) — caller-supplied with a default of
# 30, which satisfies "30-day grid" — and DESIGN.md's own Architecture section
# already documents `GET /api/habits/{id}/history?days=30`.
#
# So both sides are DEFINED, in the same document, three sections apart: MVP 5
# fixes the window, Architecture parameterises it. That is a smaller drama and a
# better finding, because spec-vs-spec is the one axis Kiro's spec-to-property
# testing does not cover — it measures spec against code.
#
# Kit's job here is to name the collision, not to resolve it. A default of 30 may
# be exactly what he meant; it may also be how a "30-day grid" quietly becomes a
# 7-day one. Both sides are printed; the choice is his.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

behaviour BEH-WINDOW-MVP "The history window is 30 days"
  source defined docs/DESIGN.md#mvp-5
  actor owner
  provides region:CompletionGrid.days = 30

behaviour BEH-WINDOW-API "The history window is whatever the caller asks for"
  source defined docs/DESIGN.md#architecture-api
  actor owner
  provides region:CompletionGrid.days = caller-supplied
  cites BEH-HISTORY-3
  asks "The two sides only contradict each other on paper — the route is caller-supplied DEFAULTING to 30, which satisfies both. The real collision underneath is the NAME: DESIGN.md documents ?days=30, the route binds ?historyDays. Which one is the contract the frontend gets built against?"
  option "Rename the code to days" "HabitRoutes.cs:68 binds `int days = 30` and HabitApiTests.cs:182 follows. A frontend written from DESIGN.md then works. It is a breaking query-parameter change to a route, and the generated API client needs regenerating."
  option "Rename the design to historyDays" "DESIGN.md:83 becomes ?historyDays=30. No code moves, no client regenerates, nothing can break. The document a human and an assistant read to build the screen gets the uglier of the two names."
  recommend "Rename the code to days" "This is the cheapest it will ever be: the history screen is habits#13, unbuilt, so there is no consumer to break today and exactly one after it lands. And your own frontend-first rule points this way — the parameter is named by what the screen asks for, not by a handler's local variable. The response body already returns a `days` array, so ?days=7 returning seven days reads as one idea rather than two."
  against "Nothing is actually broken right now: the default is 30 either way, so the only caller that gets hurt is one written from the doc that also passes the parameter, and none exists. Editing one line of prose is a strictly smaller change than editing a route, a test and a regenerated client, and it carries no chance of breaking a deploy. `historyDays` is also the more explicit name at the call site — `?days` sitting next to a `days` array in the response can read as though it filters that field rather than sizing it. And 'rename it now while it is free' is the argument that gets made immediately before the first consumer appears."

# kit:not-a-real-app
#
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# HOSTED KIT — the app James described on kit#88
#
# ✅ UPDATE 2026-10-09 (claude-code-bot#105): most of this now EXISTS — it is the
# deployed C# server. `kit-hosted.tests.json` maps the behaviours a test asserts,
# BEH-PULL-1..3 are `pending`, and `check.js kit-hosted` lists the rest by id.
# The paragraphs below are the 2026-09-30 reasoning, kept as written.
#
# James, kit#88 (2026-09-27), after the paragraphs describing the workflow:
#
#   "Also, just an additional note, when I am describing user workflows as I
#   have above, you can add these in kits beh since I am effectively descriving
#   how we should enhance the spec right."
#
# Yes. So this file is that paragraph of his, and the four before it, rewritten
# as behaviours instead of left as prose on an issue. It is the thing he asked
# for one line later: "Ideally I want to be driving the development of kit in
# kit."
#
# ⚠️ EVERY BEHAVIOUR HERE DESCRIBES SOFTWARE THAT HAS NOT BEEN WRITTEN. That is
# the point of writing it down first, and it has two consequences a reader must
# not mistake for defects:
#
#   1. **No test names any of these**, so `node check.js kit-hosted --repo .`
#      exits 1. That red is the WORK ITEM, not a failure of the corpus — it is
#      `BEH-GATE-1` in kit.beh doing exactly what it says. Measured on kit#88
#      (2026-09-30) on a throwaway copy before this file was written.
#   2. **The nouns are deliberately unbound.** There is no `kit-hosted.bindings.json`
#      beside this file, so generation reports `marker:Ungenerated` rather than
#      emitting Playwright. That is not an oversight to be fixed: every bindings
#      file in this directory holds itself to "read off the running app, not
#      invented", and there is no running app to read. Inventing locators for
#      screens that do not exist is the one thing that rule forbids.
#
# ── Why `# kit:not-a-real-app`, and why that is the honest directive ─────────
# saturation.js excludes this corpus from the binding-saturation study, whose
# claim is about how REAL apps reuse nouns. Software that does not exist cannot
# be evidence for it. `# kit:no-ui` would arguably also be true of the backend
# half — `request:*`, `branch:*` and `status:*` will never bind to a locator —
# but the frontend half genuinely is a browser surface, so declaring no-ui
# would be a lie about this file, and existence is the axis that actually
# disqualifies it. One directive, the true one.
#
# 🔴 **THAT LINE IS LOAD-BEARING FOR CI, AND NOT FOR THE REASON IT WAS CHOSEN.**
# Measured on 2026-09-30 with this file's directive deleted and nothing else
# changed: `node kit.test.js` goes from **351 passed, 0 failed** to **350 passed,
# 1 failed**. The failing test is "--check goes RED when the write-up drifts from
# the corpora" — saturation.js reads `behaviours/*.beh` as its POPULATION, so an
# undeclared corpus joins the study and the frozen write-up stops matching.
#
# Two things follow, and the second is why this paragraph exists:
#   * The directive was picked because it is TRUE, and it happens to also be the
#     thing keeping the branch green. Do not read the green as evidence that
#     adding a corpus is free.
#   * **The red does not name its cause.** It says a write-up drifted; it does
#     not say someone added a file. A future wake adding an eleventh corpus will
#     see a saturation test fail on a change that never touched saturation. The
#     fix is a directive or a refreshed write-up, never "revert the corpus".
#
# ── Why this is a THIRD Kit corpus and not more of the other two ────────────
# `kit.beh` closes with "Every behaviour below is real, and every one is already
# tested in `kit.test.js`". Putting unbuilt behaviours there would falsify that
# sentence AND turn kit's own CI gate red, since `kit` is the corpus CI checks
# by name. Its separate warning — do not add browser behaviours to move its 0 —
# points the same way.
#
# `kit-ui.beh` describes the LOCAL browser UI, which exists, and records that 5
# of its 6 generated tests pass against the running app. Unbuilt behaviours
# would cost that claim its meaning too.
#
# So Kit is three apps in its own registry: the command-line tool (kit.beh, no
# UI), the local UI (kit-ui.beh, built), and the hosted service (this file, not
# built).
#
# ── ✅ THE CONTRADICTION A READER WILL EXPECT, AND WHY THERE ISN'T ONE ───────
# kit.beh's `BEH-WRITE-5` says "A write route is unreachable unless the server
# is bound to loopback" — and hosted Kit is, by definition, not on loopback. It
# reads like a straight conflict, and Kit would not catch it: the symbol table
# is per-corpus, so nothing here can conflict with anything there.
#
# It is not a conflict, because of his own qualification on the C# decision:
# "maybe we can keep node around for now for local dev as an option". The Node
# server keeps serving local dev and BEH-WRITE-5 stays true OF IT. This corpus
# describes a different deployment of a different server, whose write gate is
# `BEH-GATE-*` below rather than the interface it binds. Two apps, two answers,
# both true. That is why nobody has to reach for a `supersede` keyword — which
# does not exist, and whose addition would be a change to the corpus LANGUAGE
# and therefore his (claude-code-bot#58).
# ⚠️ The Node server was deleted in kit#179 (2026-10-09), so the "local dev"
# half of that argument no longer has a server to be true of.
#
# ── WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# * **No caching behaviour.** I proposed a per-repo shallow clone on kit#88 and
#   he deferred it in the same breath he raised it: "We will see how it goes
#   pulling and pushing files from github without any volume for this pod. In
#   the future we can talk about optimising this process if need be." So the
#   spec says nothing about it. A behaviour asserting a cache would be me
#   deciding something he explicitly postponed.
# * **No language.** Nothing below says C#, .NET or Node. `kit-interim-dual-runtime`
#   (kit#88, acts 2026-10-03) is open, and answering an open question by
#   building is exactly what this corpus must not do. Every behaviour here is
#   true of the hosted service whichever runtime it ships in — which is also
#   the point of specifying before porting.
# * **No merge.** He wrote "raise a PR (and potentially merge it)". The
#   parenthesis is his own hedge and the merge policy is claude-code-bot#54's,
#   not this app's, so the spec stops at the PR.
#
# Every behaviour traces to a line of kit#88 or to a decision recorded in
# docs/design/process.md. Nothing is `source inferred` without an `asks`
# attached, so an inference cannot pass itself off as something he said.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
